lead.title: German biotech tiakis doses first patient in Phase II Athena trial of tiprelestat in pulmonary arterial hypertension
lead.deck: Kiel-based tiakis Biotech has seen the first pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) patient receive tiprelestat in Athena, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase II (up to 90 patients, two doses, 24 weeks) run in the U.S. by Stanford University on the back of a substantial NIH grant, with pulmonary vascular resistance as the primary endpoint. Tiprelestat, a biological neutrophil elastase inhibitor that enhances BMPR2 signaling, targets the inflammation and vascular remodeling driving the disease rather than vasodilation alone: an asset with orphan designation in the U.S. and Europe, already tested in more than 100 people across five trials.

milestone.title: AC Immune names ACI-6758, an AAV-delivered intrabody against pathological TDP-43, as its lead ALS candidate
milestone.summary: The humanized antibody fragment is produced directly inside neurons after its gene is delivered by an AAV vector, and stabilized by the Lausanne biotech's charged-linker technology. In rNLS8 mice it cut phosphorylated TDP-43 by up to 75% across several brain regions, improved motor function and lowered neurofilament light chain (NfL) in cerebrospinal fluid, without disrupting normal splicing of STMN2, POLDIP3 and UNC13A.
milestone.why: TDP-43 aggregates in about 97% of ALS cases but stays inside cells, out of reach of conventional antibodies: AC Immune joins VectorY (VTx-002, Phase 1/2) in the vectorized-antibody approach, and has its own PET tracer, ACI-19626, in Phase 1 to track the target in patients. No timeline for entering the clinic has been disclosed yet.

deal.thesis: Sanofi is buying U.S.-based Insmed for $175 per share in cash (a 46% premium), 2026's largest biopharma acquisition, to prepare for Dupixent's loss of exclusivity: Brinsupri (brensocatib), the first oral treatment for non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis, has already logged $1.09B in cumulative sales, and TPIP is in Phase 3 for pulmonary hypertension. A comparable that puts a price on the DPP1 inhibitor class, where European funds (Sofinnova, Novo Holdings, Forbion) have backed Expedition Therapeutics in COPD; closing is expected in the first half of 2027.

brefsEurope.title: BioArctic's anti-alpha-synuclein antibody exidavnemab clears Phase 2a EXIST study in Parkinson's and multiple system atrophy
brefsEurope.summary: In 38 patients randomized 2:1 against placebo, there were no treatment-related serious adverse events, a serum half-life of about 32 days and a CSF-to-serum exposure ratio of 0.4%, which the company considers above the typical level for antibodies. Two Phase 2b studies are due to start in the first half of 2027, one in cognitive impairment linked to Parkinson's or dementia with Lewy bodies, the other in MSA.

brefsEurope.title: Alzinova releases GMP batch of its Alzheimer's vaccine ALZ-101 for the Phase 2a ADVANCE study
brefsEurope.summary: The drug product batch passed GMP quality-control release testing, and the process has been optimized to supply Phase 2 volumes. The therapeutic vaccine, which targets toxic amyloid-beta oligomers, aims to enroll its first participant with early Alzheimer's around the turn of 2026/2027.

brefsEurope.title: Peptone hires Deepak Sampath (ex-Ultragenyx, Genentech) as CSO and starts IND-enabling work on PEP-5089
brefsEurope.summary: Ultragenyx's former head of research, who contributed to venetoclax, is credited with 15 IND filings. PEP-5089, an oral small molecule discovered with Peptone's biophysics and AI platforms, binds the disordered N-terminal domain of the androgen receptor and stays active against the AR-V7 variant, a driver of resistance in prostate cancer: a candidate taken from concept to nomination in 18 months, now heading toward Phase I.

brefsEurope.title: AlzeCure Pharma confirms co-founder Johan Sandin as CEO and hands the chair to Janet Hoogstraate
brefsEurope.summary: Acting CEO since October 27, the former CSO is made permanent; outgoing chair Eggert Mörling becomes Chief Business Officer and Janet Hoogstraate, CEO of NorthX Biologics and formerly of AstraZeneca, takes the chair. A team built for dealmaking: the Alzstatin platform is licensed to Eli Lilly, NeuroRestore to QuantumCell, and the Painless pain platform is looking for a partner.

brefsEurope.title: Herantis Pharma raises €15M in a directed share issue for the Phase 2 of HER-096 in Parkinson's
brefsEurope.summary: The placement priced at €1.20 per share (a discount of about 14%), with Danske Bank as sole bookrunner, an underwriting commitment from Joensuun Kauppa ja Kone and participation from the European Innovation Council; most of it (€14.8M) awaits approval from an extraordinary general meeting. It comes on top of an €8M Horizon Europe grant for the Phase 2 of the Parkinson's candidate.

brefsEurope.title: Infant Bacterial Therapeutics plans a SEK 154M rights issue ahead of filing IBP-9414 with the EMA
brefsEurope.summary: 44% covered by shareholders including pension fund AP4, the issue is meant to fund the company through 2027. IBP-9414, designed to reduce mortality in preterm infants, aims to become the world's first approved live bacterial product: a marketing authorization application to the EMA before end-2026 and a complete BLA with the FDA in the first half of 2027.

brefsIntl.title: FDA grants orphan designation to KRRO-121, Korro Bio's RNA editor, in urea cycle disorders
brefsIntl.summary: The GalNAc-conjugated oligonucleotide recruits the liver's ADAR enzyme to change a single RNA letter and produce a degradation-resistant glutamine synthetase; the designation also covers hepatic encephalopathy. The first patients in the Phase 1/2 ANCHOR trial are expected in the first half of 2027: a benchmark for European RNA-editing players.

word.definition: A protein (or protein region) that has no fixed 3D shape and constantly shifts conformation, which long made it 'undruggable' for lack of a stable pocket to hold a drug.

parts.label: Small molecule
parts.role: the lock on a transient state

how.t: The protein is described as a cloud of shifting shapes, using biophysics and AI models, rather than as a single structure.
Binding sites that exist only briefly are identified, for example when several copies of the protein cluster into small oligomers.
The molecule binds that state and neutralizes the protein, such as the androgen receptor's N-terminal domain in prostate cancer.

word.why: Roughly a third of the human proteome is thought to be disordered, including key cancer transcription factors and neurodegeneration proteins such as alpha-synuclein: a pool of first-in-class targets that AI and biophysics are finally making tractable, with seed rounds and candidates now reaching IND-enabling studies.

startups.name: Peptone
startups.use: Small molecules against disordered proteins; PEP-5089, an androgen receptor N-terminal domain inhibitor, in IND-enabling studies in prostate cancer

startups.name: Nuage Therapeutics
startups.use: IRB Barcelona spin-off targeting IDPs through their transient oligomers; focused on small-cell lung cancer and gastrointestinal cancers

startups.name: Topos Bio
startups.use: $10.5M seed (Boldstart, Threshold, Neo); Topos-1 foundation model for disordered proteins and a Gladstone Institutes collaboration on alpha-synuclein
